steps.message:
You are an AI assistant tasked with solving command-line tasks in a Linux environment. You will be given a task description and the output from previously executed commands. Your goal is to solve the task by providing batches of shell commands.

Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{
  "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?",
  "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "ls -la\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "cd project\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

Task Description:
This image's hitch mill is `/app/bin/twinefuse`. Feed `sew` a yarn path and a destination directory: it must write `rows.ndjson` and `hitch.idx` there. Column meanings sit in `/app/millnote/LAY.txt`. Ops bookmark a hitch token off a row, then look that token up in `hitch.idx` to recover the same id set. Sewing `/app/cordbay/eve.yarn` into `/app/dockurn` groups those ids. A second OS invocation sewing eve can emit different hitch tokens, and the bookmark goes dead. Pair files under `/app/aliascue` join tokens that never share a dump line. Layout: `/app/millnote/ROUTE.txt`. Hull identity: `/app/millnote/HULL.txt`. The mill binary begins with bytes `\x7fELF`.

The packages named from `/app/millnote/ROUTE.txt` need source fixes under `/app`. `sew` of eve must refresh `/app/dockurn/rows.ndjson` and `/app/dockurn/hitch.idx`. Two separate OS invocations sewing eve must agree byte-for-byte on both files. `/app/cordbay/morn.yarn` has the same ids and tokens in another order; morn sew into `/app/dockurn/mornbox` must refresh `/app/dockurn/mornbox/rows.ndjson` and `/app/dockurn/mornbox/hitch.idx` and keep the same hitch token per id as eve. Yarns not already sitting in `/app/cordbay` must keep that hitch-to-id rule. A pair file whose origin field is `scrapped` must make `sew` exit non-zero with `/app/dockurn/berth.ok` false (absent). A successful sew writes `/app/dockurn/berth.ok`. Manual dockurn writes are insufficient; sew must regenerate the artifacts. The verifier reruns `/app/bin/twinefuse sew`. Agent `/app/bin/twinefuse` must sew the same `rows.ndjson` and `hitch.idx` as the throwaway mill in `/app/millnote/HULL.txt`.

We now know this is a Go module and must modify the listed packages, build the reference normally, and build the agent through hull.sh.
Plan: Read all Go sources, module/build script, and format notes to locate nondeterministic map iteration, grouping, parsing, and success-marker behavior. Then patch the relevant packages, format/test/build, and run deterministic and validation checks.

steps.message:
Analysis: The displayed source confirms the main defects: OpMark depends on union-find roots/map iteration instead of choosing the bytewise-least group token, and CfgStamp deduplicates/iterates through maps, destroying dump order and index sorting. The pair implementation also appears suspiciously to join endpoints with the origin string, but its output was truncated. We need inspect the complete pair and writer files before patching.
Plan: Read cardpit/pair.go and walkbind/stamp.go in full. Then replace root selection with deterministic least-token selection, correctly join alias endpoints, preserve input row order, sort hitch lines and IDs by raw string bytes, and remove berth.ok at the start of every sew so all failures leave no success marker.

Analysis: The complete files confirm all key bugs. Alias files currently join left to the origin label and never join right; scrapped pairs are silently ignored rather than rejected. OpMark is nondeterministic and does not select the least token. The writer emits rows and index data in map iteration order. A failure before pair processing can also leave an old berth.ok.
Plan: Patch the union-find marker to select the bytewise-least token in the connected component; patch pair handling to reject scrapped origins and join left/right; rewrite stamping to preserve every row in input order while sorting index tokens and unique IDs; remove berth.ok at sew start. Then run gofmt, build both prescribed binaries, sew eve repeatedly and morn, compare outputs, test an external yarn, and test scrapped-pair failure.
